spec.alternative_hypothesis: The CPI step predictor has incremental predictive value for next-day SPX returns beyond SPX's own lagged return, with a Holm-adjusted p-value below 0.05, a partial R-squared of at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day SPX return predicted from its own lagged return only (BTC: its own lagged return)
cost_assumptions: The S&P 500 index is not directly tradable and no free SPX futures or ETF price series is used in this study, so the cost gate is informational, not a verdict criterion; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight
The reported gross sign-rule edge applies no costs at all and is an upper bound on any tradable edge
spec.cost_model: Informational only: the S&P 500 index is not directly tradable and no free SPX futures or ETF price series is used in this study. The trial reports the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample forecasts (no costs applied) as an informational assessment, not a verdict criterion; the out-of-sample incremental R-squared criterion carries the economic weight.
exclusions: Rows before the first calendar release (2021-01-13) have an undefined predictor and are excluded.
Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the BTC panel.
The first return row of each panel has no lag-1 predictor and is excluded.
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18 are out of sample.
The naive reference-month alignment is descriptive only and is not in the test family.
known_confounders: The CPI step predictor takes only about 70 distinct values over 2021-2026 (one per release); the roughly 1,460 daily regression rows are NOT the effective sample size. The release-day subsample test (b) is the cleaner read: each row is a fresh-information event.
The predictor is the published CPI month-on-month level, not a surprise: no consensus data is used (no free source), so this study does not measure CPI surprises.

CPIAUCSL is the current vintage: seasonal factors are revised annually, so the historical values differ slightly from the as-released prints; as-released values would need ALFRED (API key required) and the revision effect is small, but it is a stated limitation.
FRED's own posting lag for CPIAUCSL relative to the BLS release date is a second-order effect and is not modelled: the step uses the BLS release date, not the FRED posting date.

The CPI step predictor is highly autocorrelated (about 21-trading-day runs); the HAC lags are fixed in this preregistration (21 for the daily tests, 5 for the release-day subsample) and are not tuned afterwards.
Common shocks move CPI expectations and equities together; the regressions control for SPX's own lagged return only.
The BTC robustness test uses the same calendar dates as the SPX tests; the OKX bar convention (16:00 UTC open, close date = open date + 1) is handled by evaluating the step at each bar's close date.

The October 2025 CPI was never published, so the step holds the September 2025 value from 2025-10-24 until the November 2025 release on 2025-12-18 — the longest single step in the calendar, about eight weeks.
spec.mechanism: The latest published CPI print is public information; if markets under-react to the level of the latest print (rather than only to its surprise component), the print should carry incremental predictive value for next-day returns. The expected direction is negative: a higher CPI MoM tightens policy expectations and should weigh on next-day equities. The predictor is the published CPI month-on-month level, not a surprise: no consensus data is used (no free source), so this study does not measure CPI surprises.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. Rows before the first calendar release (2021-01-13) have an undefined predictor and are dropped.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with HAC standard errors (daily SPX, release-day SPX subsample, daily BTC)
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation (initial train 365 days, test 90 days, 1-day embargo), mirroring study 006
Cost gate informational only: the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample forecasts (no costs applied), with a block-bootstrap confidence interval; not a verdict criterion

Descriptive naive alignment: the same three regressions with the CPI MoM aligned by reference month (the month's value treated as known during the month, 2-6 weeks of lookahead), compared against the PIT step to quantify the lookahead bias; not in the test family
spec.multiple_testing_family: Release-day-aligned CPI transmission (3 tests: A CPI step -> next-day SPX return, B CPI step -> next-day SPX return on release-day rows only, C CPI step -> next-day BTC return)
spec.null_hypothesis: The latest published CPI MoM has no incremental predictive value for next-day returns: the step coefficient is zero and the predictor does not improve out-of-sample forecasts.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the CPI step predictor in the daily SPX lead-lag regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted A p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
spec.research_question: Does the latest published CPI month-on-month value (FRED CPIAUCSL, aligned by release date as a step function) predict next-day S&P 500 returns, and does the same predictor work on release days only and for next-day BTC returns?
spec.target_definition: Next-day close-to-close S&P 500 log return (daily primary and release-day subsample); next-day BTC-USDT perpetual log return (robustness)
spec.title: The latest published CPI MoM predicts next-day returns
